description: State, Port Authority/APM, and federal regulatory nodes extracted for the APM Elizabeth last-mile drayage pilot. Municipal rules are intentionally excluded until after Stage 4 field work. Rules rule_035 onward were added 2026-07-16 from the archived PANYNJ Marine Terminal Tariff PA-10 (effective 2026-05-01) and the guidebook's APM-specific section; these records carry optional modality and effective_from/effective_to fields. Updated 2026-07-16: N.J.A.C. 16:32 currentness resolved (expires 2029-11-30); PA-10 currentness confirmed; Elizabeth municipal rules rule_043-rule_046 added from the official Municode publication.

rules.rule_name: APM Elizabeth weekday gate opening time
rules.source_doc: APM Terminals Elizabeth Hours of Operation
rules.rule_summary: APM Terminals Elizabeth gates open Monday through Friday at 6:00 a.m.
rules.notes: Extracted from saved APM Hours of Operation PDF. Weekend and holiday hours may vary.

rules.rule_name: APM Elizabeth standard gate cutoff time
rules.source_doc: APM Terminals Elizabeth Hours of Operation
rules.source_section: Hours of Operation cutoff table, page 1
rules.rule_summary: APM Terminals Elizabeth lists a 4:00 p.m. gate cutoff for empties, the PND 921 Delancey St. empty depot, dry loads, and reefer loads.
rules.notes: Applies to listed load categories in the saved APM Hours of Operation PDF.

rules.rule_name: APM Elizabeth OOG load cutoff time
rules.source_doc: APM Terminals Elizabeth Hours of Operation
rules.source_section: Hours of Operation cutoff table, page 1
rules.rule_summary: APM Terminals Elizabeth lists a 3:30 p.m. gate cutoff for Out-of-Gauge (OOG) loads.
rules.notes: OOG loads are separated from standard load types and have an earlier cutoff.

rules.rule_name: APM Elizabeth weekend and holiday hours may vary
rules.source_doc: APM Terminals Elizabeth Hours of Operation
rules.rule_summary: APM Terminals Elizabeth states that weekend and holiday gate hours may vary, and the saved PDF includes a listed holiday schedule.
rules.notes: Holiday list appears on page 2. Temporary notices, such as special 5:00 p.m. extensions, should be treated as operational alerts rather than permanent rules.

rules.rule_name: APM Elizabeth TERMPoint appointment system
rules.source_doc: APM Terminals Elizabeth Truck Appointment System
rules.rule_summary: APM Terminals Elizabeth uses TERMPoint as the truck appointment system for managing terminal truck appointments.
rules.notes: The page presents TERMPoint as the truck appointment system and provides login/support/registration options.

rules.rule_name: TERMPoint import and export appointment scheduling
rules.source_doc: APM Terminals Elizabeth Truck Appointment System
rules.rule_summary: TERMPoint includes the ability to schedule import and export appointments, including scheduling import and export appointments simultaneously.
rules.notes: Visible on page 1 of the saved PDF. The page also references appointment availability and appointment features.

rules.rule_name: APM appointment availability may change with terminal closures
rules.source_doc: APM Terminals Elizabeth Truck Appointment System
rules.rule_summary: Appointment availability is subject to change when the terminal is closed, and changes are communicated by the terminal via e-alerts.
rules.notes: This is an operational constraint rather than a static road rule.

rules.rule_name: Marine terminal appointment prior to gate arrival
rules.authority: PANYNJ / Port of New York and New Jersey
rules.source_section: General Information — What to Have Prior to Arriving at Gate, page 3
rules.rule_summary: If visiting an applicable marine terminal, the trucker should have an appointment before arriving at the gate.
rules.notes: This is stronger than the APM TERMPoint feature page because it frames appointment status as something to have prior to gate arrival.

rules.rule_name: Driver license, TWIC, and SeaLink required before gate arrival
rules.authority: PANYNJ / Port of New York and New Jersey
rules.source_section: General Information — What to Have Prior to Arriving at Gate, page 3
rules.rule_summary: Before arriving at the gate, a trucker should have a valid driver's license, TWIC, and SeaLink identification.
rules.notes: Later federal TWIC extraction should link this local port requirement to 49 CFR Part 1572.

rules.rule_name: TWIC required for secure or restricted maritime facility access
rules.authority: TSA / U.S. Coast Guard / PANYNJ guidebook summary
rules.rule_summary: TWIC is required by federal law for workers, including drayage truck drivers, who need access to secure or restricted areas of maritime facilities.
rules.notes: This should later be cross-checked against the saved eCFR 49 CFR Part 1572 PDF.

rules.rule_name: Original TWIC must be presented for inspection
rules.authority: TSA / U.S. Coast Guard / PANYNJ guidebook summary
rules.source_section: TWIC Care and Handling Instructions, page 3
rules.rule_summary: The original TWIC must be presented for inspection when requesting unescorted access to a secure or restricted area of a marine terminal or vessel.
rules.notes: The guidebook states that presenting a photocopy instead of an actual TWIC may lead to criminal prosecution.

rules.rule_name: SeaLink mandatory for port truckers
rules.rule_summary: SeaLink is the Port Authority's uniform truck driver identification system and is mandatory for all truckers doing business at the Port of New York and New Jersey.
rules.notes: SeaLink is a driver-identification credential, separate from vehicle RFID.

rules.rule_name: SeaLink users must also have TWIC
rules.rule_summary: Anyone with SeaLink identification must also have a TWIC, and the TWIC must be registered with the Port Authority at the Truck Service Center.
rules.notes: This is a useful coupling rule because it links two credential systems.

rules.rule_name: Class 8 drayage trucks must be registered in DTR and have RFID
rules.rule_summary: All Class 8 drayage trucks seeking entry onto any Port of New York and New Jersey marine terminal must be registered in the Drayage Truck Registry and have a valid RFID tag properly mounted on the vehicle.
rules.notes: This is one of the strongest vehicle-level port access rules.

rules.rule_name: No RFID tag means no entry
rules.rule_summary: The guidebook states: no tag, no entry.
rules.notes: Short but important gate-access rule.

rules.rule_name: One RFID tag per unique vehicle
rules.rule_summary: Each unique vehicle identified by VIN/license plate must be associated with only one RFID tag in the Drayage Truck Registry, and each RFID tag must be associated with only one unique vehicle.
rules.notes: This rule matters for matching a vehicle profile to port access eligibility.

rules.rule_name: Pre-1999 truck engines denied terminal access
rules.rule_summary: Trucks with 1998 and older engine models are prohibited and will be denied access to port terminals in the Port of New York and New Jersey.
rules.notes: This is a direct engine-year rule.

rules.rule_name: 2014 EPA engine standard needed for DTR registration
rules.rule_summary: Only drayage trucks equipped with engines meeting or exceeding federal EPA on-road emission standards for 2014 model year heavy-duty diesel-fueled engines are permitted to register in the DTR via PortTruckPass.
rules.notes: This may create an important distinction between older trucks already in service and trucks attempting registration; confirm against current tariff later.

rules.rule_name: DTR access denial reasons
rules.rule_summary: Entry may be denied if the truck is not found in the DTR, has not been approved for port entry, or has a pre-1999 engine.
rules.notes: This rule directly ties vehicle registration and engine year to gate access.

rules.rule_name: UIIA registration and insurance/credit documentation before gate arrival
rules.authority: PANYNJ / Port of New York and New Jersey
rules.source_section: General Information — What to Have Prior to Arriving at Gate, page 3
rules.rule_summary: Before gate arrival, the trucking company should have proof of UIIA registration and valid insurance and credit with the steamship lines being hauled for.
rules.notes: This applies to the motor carrier/company, not just the individual truck.

rules.rule_name: Large-truck route hierarchy in New Jersey
rules.rule_summary: New Jersey establishes a roadway hierarchy for double-trailer truck combinations and 102-inch-wide standard trucks: National Network, New Jersey Access Network, and other local unrestricted roadways.
rules.notes: This is a core state routing rule for the physical-network coupling analysis. Currentness resolved 2026-07-16: Chapter 32 readopted as R.2023 d.002 effective 2022-11-30; chapter expires 2029-11-30 (NJDOT courtesy copy Supp. 1-3-23, archived at data/raw/documents/state/njac_16_32_njdot_courtesy_2026-07-16.pdf). Supersedes the expired 2022-07-02 courtesy copy.

rules.rule_name: Large trucks must use National Network except for terminal access
rules.rule_summary: Double-trailer truck combinations and 102-inch-wide standard trucks must complete trips using the National Network, but may leave the National Network to access terminals under the chapter.
rules.notes: This is the main reason the APM terminal destination matters. Currentness resolved 2026-07-16: Chapter 32 readopted as R.2023 d.002 effective 2022-11-30; chapter expires 2029-11-30 (NJDOT courtesy copy Supp. 1-3-23, archived at data/raw/documents/state/njac_16_32_njdot_courtesy_2026-07-16.pdf). Supersedes the expired 2022-07-02 courtesy copy.

rules.rule_name: Local unrestricted roadways only as necessary for terminal access
rules.rule_summary: Large trucks may use local unrestricted roadways only as necessary to access a terminal located on a local unrestricted roadway, and should return to the National Network or New Jersey Access Network by the direct route.
rules.notes: This will later be tested against the candidate path geometry. Currentness resolved 2026-07-16: Chapter 32 readopted as R.2023 d.002 effective 2022-11-30; chapter expires 2029-11-30 (NJDOT courtesy copy Supp. 1-3-23, archived at data/raw/documents/state/njac_16_32_njdot_courtesy_2026-07-16.pdf). Supersedes the expired 2022-07-02 courtesy copy.

rules.rule_name: Other state, county, and municipal restrictions still apply
rules.rule_summary: N.J.A.C. 16:32 does not supersede other state rules, municipal ordinances, or county resolutions that may restrict truck movements, including posted weight limits or local truck-route restrictions.
rules.notes: This is important because Elizabeth municipal rules and field signage can still restrict segments even if state access rules allow terminal access. Currentness resolved 2026-07-16: Chapter 32 readopted as R.2023 d.002 effective 2022-11-30; chapter expires 2029-11-30 (NJDOT courtesy copy Supp. 1-3-23, archived at data/raw/documents/state/njac_16_32_njdot_courtesy_2026-07-16.pdf). Supersedes the expired 2022-07-02 courtesy copy.

rules.rule_name: NJ Route 81 is part of the National Network near Elizabeth
rules.rule_summary: NJ Route 81 from I-95 in Elizabeth to US 1 at Newark Airport is designated as part of the National Network for double-trailer truck combinations and 102-inch-wide standard trucks.
rules.notes: Relevant because Path A begins near the NJ Turnpike/I-95/Elizabeth Seaport access area. Currentness resolved 2026-07-16: Chapter 32 readopted as R.2023 d.002 effective 2022-11-30; chapter expires 2029-11-30 (NJDOT courtesy copy Supp. 1-3-23, archived at data/raw/documents/state/njac_16_32_njdot_courtesy_2026-07-16.pdf). Supersedes the expired 2022-07-02 courtesy copy.

rules.rule_name: Terminal access documentation may demonstrate compliant routing
rules.rule_summary: When accessing terminals off the National Network, drivers may use documentation such as a bill of lading, delivery receipt, shipping order, manifest, log book, route map, written route description, or dispatcher confirmation to demonstrate compliant terminal-access routing.
rules.notes: This links freight paperwork to the route-access rule. Currentness resolved 2026-07-16: Chapter 32 readopted as R.2023 d.002 effective 2022-11-30; chapter expires 2029-11-30 (NJDOT courtesy copy Supp. 1-3-23, archived at data/raw/documents/state/njac_16_32_njdot_courtesy_2026-07-16.pdf). Supersedes the expired 2022-07-02 courtesy copy.

rules.rule_name: Commercial vehicle width limit depends on route designation
rules.source_doc: New Jersey Commercial Vehicle Size and Weight Guidebook
rules.rule_summary: Commercial vehicle width is limited to 96 inches on routes that are not National Network or NJ Access Routes, and 102 inches on National Network and NJ Access Routes.
rules.notes: This makes the truck-route designation field in physical_edges.json important.

rules.rule_name: Commercial vehicle height limit
rules.source_doc: New Jersey Commercial Vehicle Size and Weight Guidebook
rules.rule_summary: The maximum height for a commercial vehicle or combination of vehicles, including load, is 13 feet 6 inches unless otherwise identified.
rules.notes: This is why height/clearance should be captured where available in the physical network.

rules.rule_name: Trailer length depends on network/access-route status
rules.source_doc: New Jersey Commercial Vehicle Size and Weight Guidebook
rules.rule_summary: The guidebook lists different length limits by vehicle configuration and route type, including 53 feet for trailers and semitrailers on the National Network and access routes and 48 feet on other routes.
rules.notes: This should later be evaluated against whether each segment is on the National Network, NJ Access Network, or local unrestricted roadway.

rules.rule_name: OS/OW permit required when size or weight limits are exceeded
rules.source_doc: New Jersey Commercial Vehicle Size and Weight Guidebook
rules.source_section: Legal Size and Weight Limits, page 12; FAQ pages 8-9
rules.rule_summary: A vehicle or vehicle combination transporting a load that exceeds New Jersey size or weight limitations requires a special permit to move on public roads, streets, highways, or public/quasi-public property in the state.
rules.notes: This rule provides the oversize/overweight trigger used by the representative vehicle profiles.

rules.rule_name: New Jersey permit validity excludes some toll facilities without approval
rules.source_doc: New Jersey Commercial Vehicle Size and Weight Guidebook
rules.rule_summary: New Jersey permits may not be used on the New Jersey Turnpike, Garden State Parkway south of Exit 105, or Atlantic City Expressway without express approval of the tolling authority.
rules.notes: Important because Path A begins from the NJ Turnpike/Exit 13A access area.

rules.rule_name: TWIC applicants are subject to federal credentialing and security threat assessment rules
rules.rule_summary: 49 CFR Part 1572 establishes credentialing and security threat assessment regulations for certain maritime and land transportation workers, including applicants obtaining or renewing a TWIC.
rules.notes: This federal rule supports the TWIC-related PANYNJ rules already extracted.

rules.rule_name: TSA may deny or invalidate TWIC based on security threat assessment standards
rules.source_section: 49 CFR 1572.5 Standards for security threat assessments
rules.rule_summary: TSA may determine that an applicant poses a security threat warranting denial of an HME or TWIC based on disqualifying criminal offenses, immigration status requirements, security threat analysis, or mental capacity adjudication; TSA may also invalidate a TWIC immediately for immediate threats.
rules.notes: This is driver/credential eligibility, not vehicle geometry.

rules.rule_name: Large-truck map provides route-designation reference for 102-inch truck network
rules.rule_summary: The NJ Large Truck Map provides the route-designation reference used to identify National Network and NJ Access Route status for large trucks, including the 102-inch truck route network.
applies_to_segments_or_paths: North Avenue / access area pending GIS verification
rules.notes: Use this as route-designation support. Exact segment-level designation should be verified in GIS/NJDOT data before final analysis.

rules.rule_name: Tariff drayage truck deadline: DTR verification and engine-year gate denial
rules.source_doc: PANYNJ Marine Terminal Tariff PA-10 (effective May 1, 2026)
rules.source_section: Subrule 34-1140 Drayage Truck Deadline, PDF page 56
rules.rule_summary: Beginning July 2, 2023, no Container Terminal Facility shall permit access into any Port Authority terminal by a drayage truck that cannot be verified as compliant by reference to its DTR records, or by a drayage truck with an engine of model year 1998 or older. The threshold tightens to model year 1999 or older beginning May 1, 2027, and 2000 or older beginning May 1, 2028.
rules.notes: Primary current source for the engine-year and DTR gate-denial outcome previously extracted from the guidebook (rule_017, rule_019). The guidebook itself defers to the current tariff for registration and entry requirements (guidebook PDF page 4 footnote). Time-stepped thresholds are stated in the same subrule. See rule_036 for clause (c) of this subrule, recorded separately because of an interpretation problem. Currentness confirmed 2026-07-16: live PA-10 PDF byte-identical (SHA-256) to the archived 2026-05-01 edition. Version history archived (2019-06, 2022-01, 2023-01, 2024-01-01, 2025-02-10, 2026-03-10): Subrule 34-1140 clause (c) ('not an Alternative (Drayage) Truck') present in every edition since at least June 2019, annotated ISSUED 15 OCTOBER 2010. No PANYNJ erratum or clarification found as of 2026-07-16.

rules.rule_name: Tariff drayage truck deadline clause (c): literal denial of non-alternative trucks (interpretation unresolved)
rules.source_doc: PANYNJ Marine Terminal Tariff PA-10 (effective May 1, 2026)
rules.source_section: Subrule 34-1140 Drayage Truck Deadline, clause (c), PDF page 56
rules.rule_summary: Clause (c) of Subrule 34-1140 states that, beginning July 2, 2023, no Container Terminal Facility shall permit access by 'Any Drayage Truck that is not an Alternative Drayage Truck as defined in SUBRULE 34-1060'. Read literally, this denies access to every conventional diesel drayage truck.
rules.notes: Verified as the document's genuine text (repeated in the 2023, 2027, and 2028 stanzas; confirmed with layout-aware extraction). A literal reading would make clauses (a)-(b) and Subrule 34-1101's diesel DTR-registration pathway surplusage and conflicts with the guidebook's operational description of 2014+ diesel trucks doing business at the port, so a drafting error (e.g., a dropped restrictive clause tying (c) to older engines) is plausible. Do not treat as an operative denial or as a contradiction without agency clarification. Requires human/agency review. Currentness confirmed 2026-07-16: live PA-10 PDF byte-identical (SHA-256) to the archived 2026-05-01 edition. Version history archived (2019-06, 2022-01, 2023-01, 2024-01-01, 2025-02-10, 2026-03-10): Subrule 34-1140 clause (c) ('not an Alternative (Drayage) Truck') present in every edition since at least June 2019, annotated ISSUED 15 OCTOBER 2010. No PANYNJ erratum or clarification found as of 2026-07-16.

interpretation_evidence.literal_reading: Clause (c) read literally denies terminal access to every drayage truck that is not an Alternative Drayage Truck (34-1060: LNG/CNG/electric/qualifying hybrid only) since 2023-07-02.
against_literal_operativeness: Clause present since at least June 2019 tied to earlier deadlines (2020-08-01); conventional diesel drayage demonstrably continued after each deadline.
Subrule 34-1101 (same instrument, same date) creates a diesel registration pathway (MY2014+ EPA standard) that would be surplusage under a literal (c).
Subrule 34-1120 sticker schedule treats '1998 and Newer' diesels and 'Alternative Drayage Trucks' as parallel compliant categories.

PANYNJ operational statement (drayage-truck-registration page, mirrored by US DOE AFDC): MY2014+ standard required for terminal access; alternative-fuel trucks are EXEMPT from these requirements - i.e., an exemption category, not the exclusive permitted class.
APM Terminals operates a working diesel truck appointment system (TERMPoint) as of 2026-07-16.
for_literal_operativeness: The clause is genuine, current tariff text, repeated in the 2023, 2027, and 2028 stanzas of the current edition.
interpretation_evidence.named_blocker: PANYNJ authoritative clarification, erratum, or superseding PA-10 text resolving Subrule 34-1140(c), checked as of 2026-07-16.

rules.rule_name: Tariff DTR registration limited to 2014 EPA standard engines
rules.source_doc: PANYNJ Marine Terminal Tariff PA-10 (effective May 1, 2026)
rules.source_section: Subrule 34-1101 Registration in Drayage Truck Registry (DTR), PDF page 56
rules.rule_summary: Beginning July 2, 2023, only drayage trucks equipped with an engine that meets or exceeds federal EPA on-road emission standards for engine model year 2014 heavy-duty diesel-fueled engines shall be permitted to complete registration in the DTR via the PortTruckPass website.
rules.notes: Primary current source for the registration standard previously extracted from the guidebook (rule_018). Governs registration in the DTR, which is a different act from gate entry (rule_035); trucks registered before this standard applied are not addressed by this subrule's text. Currentness confirmed 2026-07-16: live PA-10 PDF byte-identical (SHA-256) to the archived 2026-05-01 edition. Version history archived (2019-06, 2022-01, 2023-01, 2024-01-01, 2025-02-10, 2026-03-10): Subrule 34-1140 clause (c) ('not an Alternative (Drayage) Truck') present in every edition since at least June 2019, annotated ISSUED 15 OCTOBER 2010. No PANYNJ erratum or clarification found as of 2026-07-16.

rules.rule_name: Tariff gate access: terminals must verify DTR compliance
rules.source_doc: PANYNJ Marine Terminal Tariff PA-10 (effective May 1, 2026)
rules.rule_summary: All Container Terminal Facilities shall have installed appropriate means of accessing the Port's Drayage Truck Registry to obtain relevant information to confirm a drayage truck's compliance with Container Terminal Facility access requirements under the tariff.
rules.notes: Obligation on the terminal operator, not the truck. Establishes that DTR status is checked at the gate. Currentness confirmed 2026-07-16: live PA-10 PDF byte-identical (SHA-256) to the archived 2026-05-01 edition. Version history archived (2019-06, 2022-01, 2023-01, 2024-01-01, 2025-02-10, 2026-03-10): Subrule 34-1140 clause (c) ('not an Alternative (Drayage) Truck') present in every edition since at least June 2019, annotated ISSUED 15 OCTOBER 2010. No PANYNJ erratum or clarification found as of 2026-07-16.

rules.rule_name: Tariff definition: Alternative Drayage Trucks
rules.source_doc: PANYNJ Marine Terminal Tariff PA-10 (effective May 1, 2026)
rules.source_section: Subrule 34-1060 Alternative Drayage Trucks, PDF page 55
rules.rule_summary: 'Alternative Drayage Trucks' are drayage trucks with heavy-duty engines operating on liquefied or compressed natural gas, electricity, or hybrid technology, including qualifying pilot-ignition engines limited to no more than one part diesel to ten parts total fuel; engines that can operate or idle solely on diesel fuel at any time do not meet the definition.
rules.notes: Definition referenced by Subrule 34-1140 clause (c) (rule_036). Not an operative rule by itself. Currentness confirmed 2026-07-16: live PA-10 PDF byte-identical (SHA-256) to the archived 2026-05-01 edition. Version history archived (2019-06, 2022-01, 2023-01, 2024-01-01, 2025-02-10, 2026-03-10): Subrule 34-1140 clause (c) ('not an Alternative (Drayage) Truck') present in every edition since at least June 2019, annotated ISSUED 15 OCTOBER 2010. No PANYNJ erratum or clarification found as of 2026-07-16.

rules.rule_name: Tariff definition: Drayage Truck Registry (DTR)
rules.source_doc: PANYNJ Marine Terminal Tariff PA-10 (effective May 1, 2026)
rules.source_section: Subrule 34-1080 Drayage Truck Registry, PDF page 55
rules.rule_summary: The DTR is a database of trucks authorized by the Port Authority to conduct business at Port Authority terminals, recording owner contact details and vehicle make, model year, engine make/model/model year, VIN, GVWR, and license information.
rules.notes: Definition supporting rule_035, rule_037, and rule_038. Not an operative rule by itself. Currentness confirmed 2026-07-16: live PA-10 PDF byte-identical (SHA-256) to the archived 2026-05-01 edition. Version history archived (2019-06, 2022-01, 2023-01, 2024-01-01, 2025-02-10, 2026-03-10): Subrule 34-1140 clause (c) ('not an Alternative (Drayage) Truck') present in every edition since at least June 2019, annotated ISSUED 15 OCTOBER 2010. No PANYNJ erratum or clarification found as of 2026-07-16.

rules.rule_name: All gate moves at APM Terminals require an appointment
rules.source_section: APM Terminals section, printed pages 18-19 (PDF page 11)
rules.rule_summary: The guidebook's APM Terminals section states: 'ALL GATE MOVES AT APMT REQUIRE AN APPOINTMENT', with all appointments made on the TERMPoint website or app; appointments cannot be created, modified, or merged after the trucker passes through inbound OCR.
rules.notes: Stronger and APMT-specific compared with rule_005/rule_006 (system descriptions) and rule_008 (generic 'applicable marine terminal' phrasing). The archived guidebook shows no publication date; treat currentness as a limitation.

rules.rule_name: Mandatory APM safety induction training for terminal access
rules.source_section: APM Terminals section, Mandatory Trucker Training, printed pages 18-19 (PDF page 11)
rules.rule_summary: All truck drivers are required to complete the mandatory online safety induction video/quiz in order to access the APM terminal. Induction status is tied to the driver's SeaLink number; a new SeaLink card requires retaking the induction, while switching companies with the same SeaLink number does not.
rules.notes: Corroborated by the archived APM Truck Appointment System page (PDF page 2), which surfaces drivers' Safety Induction status in TERMPoint 'to avoid turnaround at the Inbound gate'. Undated guidebook; treat currentness as a limitation.

rules.rule_name: Elizabeth 4-ton gross-weight exclusion streets (corridor streets not listed)
rules.rule_summary: Trucks over 4 tons gross weight are excluded from the streets enumerated in 10.16.010 except for pickup and delivery on such street. The enumerated schedule does not include North Avenue, North Avenue East, McLester Street, Tripoli Street, Kapkowski Road, or Dowd Avenue.
rules.notes: Included so the corridor negative finding is testable in the pair scan. Couples to no modeled corridor edge. Extracted 2026-07-16 from the official Municode publication (Supp. 31); also recorded in municipal_rules_verified.json.

rules.rule_name: Elizabeth 80,000-lb overweight-vehicle zone on North Avenue East (permissive port connection)
rules.source_section: 10.16.050 An 80,000 pound overweight vehicle zone limit—Streets affected (Ord. 4654, 2015-12-22)
rules.rule_summary: Designates an over-80,000-lb overweight vehicle zone on North Avenue East beginning 440 feet east of the Kapkowski Road intersection and continuing 520 feet east to the vacated portion of North Avenue East and its connection to the Port Authority overweight vehicle zone.
applies_to_segments_or_paths: North Avenue East (440-960 ft east of Kapkowski Rd)
rules.notes: Permissive zone designation connecting to the Port Authority overweight vehicle zone; not a prohibition on legal-weight trucks. Extracted 2026-07-16 from the official Municode publication (Supp. 31); also recorded in municipal_rules_verified.json.

rules.rule_name: Elizabeth overnight truck parking prohibition (parking act only)
rules.source_section: 10.40.020 No parking of certain vehicles from 9:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m.; 10.40.090 no truck parking near schools/parks
rules.rule_summary: Prohibits parking of trucks/commercial vehicles on city streets 9:00 p.m.-6:00 a.m. (with exceptions) and at all times near listed schools/parks (one listed zone borders a midtown block of North Avenue East near Kellogg Park). Governs the act of parking only, not roadway operation or terminal entry.
rules.notes: Recorded to keep the parking act separate from operating restrictions per project rule. Cannot contradict operating or entry rules (different act). Extracted 2026-07-16 from the official Municode publication (Supp. 31); also recorded in municipal_rules_verified.json.

rules.rule_name: Elizabeth traffic-control devices on corridor intersections (signal/stops)
rules.source_section: 10.08 schedules: signal at North Avenue East & Kapkowski Road; three-way stop at Dowd Avenue & York Street
rules.rule_summary: Establishes traffic-control devices (signal, stop signs) at corridor intersections. Imposes ordinary traffic control, not a truck prohibition or truck route restriction.
applies_to_segments_or_paths: North Avenue East & Kapkowski Road intersection
rules.notes: Included for completeness of the municipal movement layer on the corridor. Extracted 2026-07-16 from the official Municode publication (Supp. 31); also recorded in municipal_rules_verified.json.
